text: Ensuring security is a critical part of building any website. One of the first steps is to use HTTPS, which encrypts data sent between the user’s browser and the server, protecting sensitive information from being intercepted. Another essential practice is implementing strong authentication, such as requiring complex passwords and using multi-factor verification, to confirm that users are who they claim to be. Additionally, developers must validate all user input, because failing to do so can lead to common vulnerabilities like SQL injection or cross-site scripting, where attackers can steal data or take control of the site. By focusing on these areas, developers can create safer, more trustworthy web applications.
